title: Temporary access code serves as identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user can serve as a unique reference to identify the data subject's access event, potentially linking the guest to the home system.
assumptions: The access code is logged and associated with the guest user's identity in the system.

title: Access code may be more sensitive than functionally required
description: The temporary access code is a sensitive credential that may be collected and processed beyond what is strictly needed for the door unlocking function.
assumptions: The system stores or logs the access code beyond the immediate unlocking event.

title: Access code may be retained longer than functionally needed
description: The temporary access code may be stored or logged for longer than necessary for the door unlocking functionality, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: The system retains access code logs for audit or historical purposes.

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest user may not be aware that their temporary access code is being logged, stored, or processed by the home hub system.
assumptions: No clear privacy notice or consent mechanism is provided to the guest user.

title: Guest lacks control over access code processing
description: The guest user has limited control over how their temporary access code is processed, stored, or shared by the home hub system.
assumptions: No mechanism exists for the guest to opt-out or control data retention of their access code.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing the temporary access code may violate GDPR data minimization principle if the code is collected or stored beyond what is strictly necessary for door unlocking.
assumptions: The system collects and processes more personal data than functionally required.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video clips uploaded from Home Hub may contain metadata with unique identifiers (device IDs, user IDs, timestamps) that can link video data to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of video content attributes (location, time, people visible) with metadata can serve as quasi-identifiers to link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video content combined with metadata creates linkable profile

title: Processing of identified personal data
description: Video clips contain personal data about individuals in the home environment, which is identified and processed during upload to cloud storage.
assumptions: Video content captures identifiable individuals

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content reveals revealing attributes about data subjects including appearance, activities, location, and interactions that support identification.
assumptions: Video captures identifiable personal attributes

title: Small anonymity set allows singling out
description: In a home context, the number of individuals visible in video is small, making it easy to single out specific data subjects from the video content.
assumptions: Home video typically shows limited number of individuals

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: Video footage is highly sensitive personal data that captures private activities and may be perceived as more sensitive than functionally required for basic storage.
assumptions: Video is inherently sensitive personal data

title: Data propagation to cloud services
description: Video data is propagated to cloud storage services where it may be accessible by additional parties beyond the immediate user.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves third-party service providers

title: Excessive party involvement in data access
description: Cloud video storage may make data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including cloud service providers, support staff, or law enforcement.
assumptions: Cloud storage involves multiple access parties

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their video footage is being uploaded to cloud storage, processed, and potentially retained.
assumptions: Users may not understand full data processing implications

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may have limited control over how their video data is processed, stored, and potentially shared with third parties.
assumptions: User consent mechanisms may be insufficient

title: Difficulty in rectification or erasure of video data
description: Data subjects may face challenges in requesting deletion or correction of video data stored in cloud systems.
assumptions: Cloud storage retention policies may be rigid

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video recording may capture more personal data than functionally necessary for the stated purpose of home security or monitoring.
assumptions: Full video recording exceeds minimal necessary data collection

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be retained in cloud storage longer than functionally necessary, exceeding legal retention requirements.
assumptions: Cloud storage retention may exceed necessary duration

title: Quasi-identifier in motion alert data
description: Motion alert data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., timestamp, location, device ID) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion alerts include metadata that can be combined to identify individuals
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion alerts contain identifiable metadata

title: Excessive data granularity in motion alerts
description: Real-time motion alerts may be transmitted with finer granularity than functionally required, potentially revealing more detailed information about user behavior than necessary.
assumptions: Motion data granularity exceeds functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Assuming motion data is more granular than needed

title: Excessive frequency of motion data processing
description: Real-time motion alerts are processed and transmitted at high frequency, potentially more often than functionally necessary for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Real-time transmission frequency exceeds functional requirements

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected and forwarded to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users are not informed about motion data collection

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences regarding how their motion data is collected, processed, and shared.
assumptions: No granular consent controls for motion data

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Motion data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the functional purpose of alerting the mobile app.
assumptions: Data collection exceeds functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Assuming data minimization is not properly implemented

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Motion alert data is shared with the mobile app backend, which may be a predetermined set of parties beyond what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: Data sharing extends beyond immediate functional need
uncertainty_note: Assuming data sharing scope may be broader than needed

title: Linking through unique identifier in notification
description: The motion-detected notification likely contains the homeowner's unique identifier (e.g., user ID, phone number) to route the notification to the correct recipient, enabling linking of the notification to a specific individual.
assumptions: The notification includes identifying information to deliver to the correct homeowner.

title: Profiling an individual through motion detection data
description: Motion detection data can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's habits, routines, and presence patterns at the property, potentially revealing sensitive information about their lifestyle.
assumptions: Motion detection data is collected and stored over time, enabling pattern analysis.

title: Processing of identified data for notification delivery
description: The system processes identified data (homeowner's identifier) to deliver the motion-detected notification to the correct recipient.
assumptions: The notification system requires homeowner identification to route messages.

title: Revealing attributes through motion detection
description: Motion detection data reveals attributes such as time of day, location, and frequency of presence at the property, which can support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: Motion detection data includes temporal and location information.

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected at the property, making the detection observable to the homeowner and potentially others.
assumptions: The notification is sent to the homeowner's device, making the detection event observable.

title: Excessive data type granularity in notification
description: The notification may include more granular data (e.g., precise timestamp, specific location) than functionally needed for a simple motion alert.
assumptions: The notification includes detailed motion detection metadata beyond what's needed for basic alerting.

title: Unnecessary treatment of motion detection data
description: Motion detection data may be analyzed, enriched, or processed beyond what is necessary to achieve the functional goal of sending a notification.
assumptions: The system performs additional processing on motion data beyond simple notification delivery.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how motion detection data is collected, processed, and potentially used beyond notification delivery.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly disclose all uses of motion detection data.

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: The homeowner may lack control to set preferences regarding how motion detection data is collected, processed, or shared.
assumptions: The system does not provide granular consent or preference controls for motion data.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data (e.g., detailed motion patterns, timestamps) than is actually needed for the functional goal of sending a motion notification.
assumptions: The system collects and processes motion data beyond what's necessary for basic notification functionality.
